cards.text: Pull up a stool, friend. John is writing to believers he calls little children, and he's just warned them about people trying to deceive them (1 John 2:26). Now he says it plain: remain in Christ, because one day He appears.

cards.question: John tells the little children to remain in Christ. What does he want for them when Christ appears?

answers.text: To be confident and unashamed before Him
To be the very first ones He greets
To be given more than everyone else

cards.text: Then John reasons it out like a dad at the kitchen table. If you know He is righteous, you also know something about everyone who practices righteousness.

cards.question: True or false: John says everyone who practices righteousness has been born of Him.

cards.text: Then John just STOPS, and I think he can't get over it: look at the love the Father has given us! Friend, I came out of a bin with a 25-cent sticker on me, so I know a LITTLE something about getting picked up when nobody had to.

cards.question: Because of the love the Father has given, what does John say believers are called?
True or false: John says being called children of God is only a title and not what believers really are.

cards.text: But heads up, friend. John says the world does not know us, and he says there's a reason for that.

cards.question: Why does John say the world doesn't know God's children?

cards.text: We're children of God right NOW, John says, but what we will be hasn't been revealed yet. It's like staring through the oven door at a batch: you KNOW it's cookies, you just haven't seen the finished thing.

cards.question: What does John say God's children will be when Christ appears?
True or false: John says believers will be like Christ because they will see Him as He is.

cards.text: Now THAT is a hope worth holding onto. And John says it doesn't just sit on the counter but gets to work on the person who has it.

cards.question: Everyone who has this hope in Christ ___ himself, just as Christ is pure.

cards.text: Now John turns to sin, and he does NOT tiptoe. He says straight out what sin is.

cards.question: John says plainly that sin is ___.

cards.text: But John reminds them of something they already know. Christ appeared, and He came for a reason.

cards.question: Why does John say Christ appeared?

answers.text: To give a new set of laws
To set up His throne in Jerusalem

cards.question: True or false: John says there is no sin in Christ.

cards.text: Then John draws a line: no one who remains in Him keeps on sinning. Now, I REMAINED in the back of a junk drawer for years, but friend, that is a VERY different kind of remaining.

cards.question: What does John say about someone who continues to sin?

answers.text: He has not seen or known Christ
He is closer to Christ than he thinks
He only needs one more warning

cards.text: John's calling them little children again, and he's got a warning for them: don't let anyone deceive you.

cards.question: The one who practices ___ is righteous, just as Christ is righteous.

cards.text: Then John goes all the way back. The one who practices sin is of the devil, he says, because the devil has been sinning from the very start.

cards.question: True or false: John says the Son of God was revealed to destroy the works of the devil.

cards.text: Anyone born of God refuses to practice sin, John says, and he can't go on sinning. It's like my stamp: press me into the dough and you get Papa Dorin EVERY time, mustache and all, because of what's on me.

cards.question: Why does John say someone born of God won't keep practicing sin?

cards.text: So how do you tell the children of God from the children of the devil? John says anyone who does not practice righteousness is not of God.

cards.question: John gives one more sign that someone is not of God. What is it?

answers.text: He does not love his brother
He does not know the law
He does not keep the feasts

findings.problem: The card says 'remain in Christ, because one day He appears.' That gives a reason the text doesn't give. 1 John 2:28 says to remain in Christ 'so that when He appears, we may be confident and unashamed before Him.' The purpose is to be confident and unashamed, not the fact that He appears.

rule.text: **Reasons.** He never adds why someone did, said or thought something unless the text says why.

findings.problem: The card says the hope 'gets to work on the person who has it,' which makes the hope do the purifying. 1 John 3:3 says the person 'purifies himself.' The retelling moves the action from the person to the hope.

rule.text: **Retelling:** Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: The blank answer gives itself away inside its own sentence: 'The one who practices ___ is righteous, just as Christ is righteous.' 'righteousness' echoes 'righteous' twice, so it stands out against 'tradition' and 'patience' without any reasoning. The card also asks about wording rather than the warning against being deceived that the story card set up.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: The right answer 'God's seed abides in him' uses Bible wording ('abides'). The wrong answers are casual and modern ('He's afraid of getting caught', 'He's never tempted again'), so the right answer stands out by tone.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: Papa Dorin's humor is mostly mild across the walkthrough. Several cards read like a nice dad being pleasant rather than laugh-out-loud funny: stop 1 card 3 ('like a dad at the kitchen table'), stop 1 card 10 (the oven door line), stop 1 card 13, stop 2 card 12 ('mustache and all'). Many story cards could hold a real laugh without muddying a fact but don't try.

rule.text: **But he is FUNNY.** Not mildly amusing. Laugh-out-loud funny, the kind a baker repeats to a friend. Because he talks naturally, the funny moments come up a lot: in his reactions, his comparisons, his disbelief and his self-deprecation. When a moment can hold a real laugh without muddying a fact, he goes for it. If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.

findings.problem: The card names 'John' as the letter's writer with no introduction and no reference. 1 John never names its author, so there is no verse to cite for who John is. The New People rule asks for a simple introduction, and outside facts like who wrote a letter need a reference.
findings.question: For a letter that doesn't name its author, like 1 John, how should Papa Dorin introduce the writer? Should he name 'John' with a short description, such as one of Jesus' twelve apostles, with no reference? Should he just say 'the writer'? Or something else?
